transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hey, doc. Thanks. Yeah, so... I guess what brings me in is things are just getting really bad for me at work. I'm a construction manager, and I'll sit down to do a plan review, or I'll start running a safety briefing for the guys, and I am trying so hard to just pay attention to what's right in front of me. 

But I swear, within minutes, my mind is completely off on three other job problems. Like yesterday, we had this massive holdup with the drywall crew. The foreman, Jimmy, he always shows up late. He drives this beat-up old Ford that actually reminds me of the truck my dad used to have. Man, that thing was a piece of junk, the transmission blew out on us right in the middle of a family road trip down to Florida when I was a kid... 

But, uh, wait, what was I saying? Right, the safety briefings and the plans. So because my head is always bouncing around to all these other issues on the site, I end up missing things in the reviews that I absolutely know I should have caught. It's becoming a real liability.
Have you always had trouble paying attention like this, or is this a relatively recent problem for you?

Oh, man, no, this isn't new at all. It's been my whole life. Like, way back in elementary school, the teachers were already telling my parents I was a handful. They told them I couldn't stay in my seat, and I was always talking out of turn. 

I remember I had Mrs. Higgins for third grade, and she had this rule where you had to hold up this little wooden pass if you wanted to speak. It was shaped like a parrot. My buddy Mike actually broke the parrot once by dropping it on the radiator. The school had those old, clanking cast-iron radiators that would practically cook you if you sat too close. Mike ended up moving to Ohio in middle school, actually. Good guy, I think he runs a roofing business out there now. We should probably catch up...

But yeah, the teachers would call my folks all the time because I constantly lost my homework. And whenever we had an assignment, I just rushed through the directions before I really even understood what they wanted me to do. I just wanted to get it over with, you know? We used to play wall-ball against the side of the cafeteria and I wanted to be first out the door... 

Wait, sorry. I'm doing it again, aren't I? What was your question?
Do you often feel restless or fidgety, like you need to get up and move around?

Yeah, absolutely. It's like I have this motor inside me that just won't shut off. Like, we have these big production meetings on Tuesday mornings, right? And everybody else can just sit there in those cheap plastic chairs for an hour straight. But I can't do it. I'm always the guy standing up, pacing around the back of the trailer, walking over to grab another cup of coffee, or making some excuse to step outside and check on a delivery. 

Actually, speaking of deliveries, we had this flatbed show up last week with the wrong grade of lumber. The driver was this older guy, had a huge white beard, looked exactly like Santa Claus. I asked him where he came from, and he said he drove all the way down from Maine. I went to Maine once when I was a teenager, we stayed in this cabin right on a lake... the mosquitoes were unbelievable, just massive. We spent half the trip swatting bugs instead of fishing. 

Anyway... yeah, sitting still. It's just... I always have to be moving, you know? I just can't stay glued to a chair like everyone else.
Do you feel like your trouble paying attention and restlessness are causing problems for you in your personal relationships or at home, not just at work?

Oh, man, yeah. It's bleeding into everything. At work, it actually just came to a head. My site coordination has been so disorganized lately, and I keep missing these important follow-ups with the subcontractors, that my boss actually issued a formal concern. He pulled me into the main office for it. 

The main office is over on 4th street, right next to this incredible Italian sub shop. I used to go there like three times a week when we were building the bank down the block. The guy who runs it, Tony, he makes his own giardiniera from scratch, it's so spicy it'll make your eyes water. I actually tried growing hot peppers in my backyard last summer to make my own, but the rabbits got to them. Rabbits are a huge menace in our neighborhood, they just chew through the chicken wire like it's nothing. My neighbor actually bought this fake owl to scare them away, but I swear the birds just end up sitting on its head... 

Wait, sorry, I lost the thread again. You asked about home, right? Yeah, my wife... she's just completely worn down. I'll promise her I'm going to handle something around the house, and I really mean to do it, but then it just completely leaves my brain. So she ends up having to remind me over and over again about things I already said I'd handle, and I know she's just sick of having to manage me on top of everything else.
Do you often interrupt others or blurt out answers before they finish speaking?

Yeah, definitely. It's bad. I always cut people off because it's like my brain is just moving too fast, so I think I already know exactly where their question is going. I just jump right in. 

Like, just yesterday, my lead electrician, Dave, came up to me on site. I immediately started telling him about the clearance for the HVAC ducts because I assumed that's what he was going to ask about. The HVAC guys on this job have been a total nightmare, by the way. They parked their van right in front of the cement mixer on Tuesday. It’s a brand new Ford Transit, too, custom wrapped with their logo. I don't know why you'd spend that much on a vinyl wrap for a work van. My buddy runs a detailing shop and he says those wraps start peeling after a year anyway if you don't keep them out of the sun. He's got a shop out on Route 9, right past the old drive-in theater that closed down last year. Man, I miss that drive-in. We took the kids there to see a movie a few summers ago, and the popcorn was always super stale but it was just a fun time, you know? They’re supposed to be turning that lot into a strip mall now, which we really don't need... 

Wait, sorry, I'm rambling again. But yeah, with Dave, I answered him way too fast, and then I realized I completely missed the important part of what he was actually saying. He hadn't even gotten to it yet—he was actually trying to warn me about a live wire they found behind the drywall. So, yeah. I jump the gun a lot.
Do you feel like your symptoms are affecting your overall quality of life?

Yeah, I mean, like I was saying earlier, it's really taking a toll on everything. My overall quality of life is just... it's really stressful right now. Like I mentioned about work, getting that formal concern from my employer because my site coordination has been a mess and I keep missing follow-ups... that really shook me. I've been doing this a long time, so having my boss sit me down like that is tough. 

And then at home, like I said, my wife is just so worn down from having to remind me about every little thing I promised I'd handle. Actually, just this weekend I was supposed to fix the gutter on the garage. The rain just pours right over it, and we had a huge storm last month that flooded half the street. The drainage in our neighborhood is an absolute joke. The city sent these public works guys out a few weeks ago, and they just stood around looking at the storm drain for like three hours. One of them was driving this old Chevy C10 truck, had to be a '78 or '79. Beautiful truck, cherry red. My dad had one almost exactly like it when I was a kid. We used to ride in the bed on the way to the town dump on Saturday mornings... you could never do that now, the cops would pull you over in a second. Everything is so strict now with safety rules. I mean, OSHA is all over our job sites lately, you practically gotta wear a hard hat just to use the porta-john... 

Anyway, sorry, what was I saying? Right, my life. Yeah, it's definitely affecting my life. Between the situation with my boss and my wife just being totally exhausted by me, I just feel like I'm constantly letting everyone down because I can't keep my head straight.
Did you experience these same symptoms of inattention and restlessness when you were a teenager, similar to when you were in elementary school?

Oh, yeah, absolutely. It's been this way for as long as I can remember. Even back in elementary school, my teachers were constantly pulling my parents aside, telling them I couldn't stay in my seat, I was always talking out of turn, losing my homework... I'd just rush through the directions on assignments before I even knew what I was supposed to be doing. 

Actually, my third-grade teacher, Mrs. Gable, she used to have this big jar of marbles on her desk. Every time the class was good, she'd put a marble in, and when it was full we'd get a pizza party. I swear I was the reason that jar never filled up. She had this crazy collection of porcelain frogs, too. Like, everywhere in the classroom. On the windowsills, by the chalkboard... I knocked one over once when I was supposed to be reading quietly but I was trying to balance my pencil on my nose instead. It shattered into a million pieces. My mom had to go to this antique store downtown to find a replacement. That antique store is still there, actually. It's run by this guy who repairs old grandfather clocks. The craftsmanship on those things is insane, all those little gears and weights. I always thought it would be cool to learn how to build something like that, but you need so much patience. I tried building a model airplane once with my son, one of those B-17 bombers, and I glued my thumb to the fuselage within the first ten minutes...

Wait, what was the question? Oh, right, being a teenager. Yeah, it was the exact same stuff in high school, too. The restlessness, not paying attention... it just never really stopped.
Are you finding it harder to enjoy activities or spend time with family and friends because of your trouble paying attention and restlessness?

Yeah, I mean, I guess so. It's definitely harder to just sit back and enjoy things. Like, even when I'm trying to hang out with my buddies or be with the family, my mind is just going a million miles an hour. I can't just relax. We had some friends over for a barbecue on Sunday, and I spent the whole time pacing around the yard, messing with the grill, checking my phone... 

Speaking of the grill, I just bought this new smoker. It's one of those pellet ones, you know? Supposed to keep a perfect temperature for like twelve hours straight. I was trying to smoke a brisket, and you really gotta watch the internal temp on those. The guy at the butcher shop told me the secret is wrapping it in butcher paper halfway through, not foil. Foil traps the steam and ruins the bark. That butcher shop is amazing, by the way. It's this old-school Italian place, they make their own sausage right there in the back. The spicy Italian one is incredible. My wife can't handle the spice, though. She gets heartburn if she even looks at a red pepper. She's been taking those antacids like candy lately. I keep telling her she needs to go see a doctor about it, but she hates going to the doctor. Her dad was the same way, stubborn as a mule. He wouldn't go to the hospital even when he broke his toe dropping a cinder block on it...

Wait, sorry, what were we talking about? Oh, enjoying things. Yeah, I don't know, it's just tough to stay in the moment with people. I'm always just... itching to do something else, I guess.
Are you feeling like your symptoms are causing problems in your relationships with friends, not just family?

Yeah, I guess so. I mean, my friends definitely notice it. I've known most of these guys since high school, so they're used to me being all over the place, but lately it feels like they're getting a little... I don't know, annoyed? Like, we go to this sports bar every Thursday for wings and to watch whatever game is on. It's this place called The Dugout, over by the old mall. The wings are decent, but they have this garlic parmesan sauce that is just... man, it's out of this world. They actually changed management a few months ago, and the new owner completely redid the interior. Took down all the old neon signs and put up these huge flat screens. Which is great for the games, but they painted the walls this weird shade of gray. It looks like a dentist's office now. My dentist, Dr. Patel, he just retired last year. Moved down to Florida, bought a boat. I can't even imagine living on a boat. The maintenance on the hull alone... saltwater just eats right through everything. You gotta constantly scrape the barnacles off and repaint it. I knew a guy who worked at a marina, and he said the fiberglass repair jobs they'd get were just nightmare fuel... 

Wait, what was the question? Oh, my friends. Right. Yeah, so at the bar, I'm constantly getting up, checking my phone, going outside, interrupting them when they're trying to tell a story... I can tell they're getting frustrated with me. One of them even made a joke last week about putting a leash on me so I'd stay at the table. So yeah, I'd say it's causing some friction.
Are there any situations or activities where you feel your symptoms are so severe that they completely disrupt your ability to function or interact with others?

Yeah, it's definitely getting to that point, honestly. Like, at work, it's becoming a real issue. I'm a construction manager, right? So I'm supposed to be coordinating all these different crews, making sure materials arrive on time, keeping everything on schedule. But lately, I'm just dropping the ball. I'll forget to follow up with the electricians, or I'll double-book a site for two different deliveries... It got so bad recently that my boss actually pulled me into his office for a formal sit-down. He was really concerned. 

And, you know, being in construction, the supply chain stuff right now is just a nightmare anyway. Trying to get your hands on a decent batch of lumber? Forget about it. Prices are through the roof. I was at the lumberyard the other day, and the guy running the forklift—I've known him for years, big guy named Sal—he was telling me they had a whole shipment of plywood held up at the port for three weeks. Just sitting there. It's crazy how much of our stuff comes through those ports. I watched this documentary once about container ships, and the logistics involved are just mind-blowing. They have these massive cranes that can unload a ship in hours. The guy who invented the shipping container, he completely revolutionized global trade. Before that, everything was just loaded onto ships in barrels and sacks by hand. Can you imagine the back labor? My uncle used to work on the docks in Philly back in the seventies, and he had the worst back problems. He ended up having to get two surgeries, and they put all these metal rods in his spine. He used to set off the metal detectors at the airport every single time...

Wait, sorry. The question. Disrupting things. Yeah, so work is bad, and at home, it's not much better. My wife is just completely worn down. I'll tell her I'm gonna handle something—like fixing the leaky faucet or paying the water bill—and I just completely forget. She has to constantly remind me, and I know it's exhausting for her. It's like I can't function normally without her managing me, and I hate that.
Are you feeling overwhelmed or distressed by your inability to focus and stay on task?

Yeah, I mean... distressed is a good word for it. Overwhelmed, definitely. It's like I'm drowning in my own head sometimes. I know what I need to do, but I just can't make myself do it, or I start and then I'm off doing something else entirely. It's incredibly frustrating. 

Like yesterday, I was supposed to be reviewing these blueprints for a new commercial build. It's a really interesting project, actually—they're repurposing this old textile mill downtown into loft apartments and retail space. The brickwork on that building is phenomenal. You just don't see craftsmanship like that anymore. Everything now is just pre-fab panels and cheap drywall. I was talking to this mason the other day, older guy, and he was telling me about the different types of mortar they used to use back in the early 1900s. Apparently, there's this specific ratio of lime to sand that allows the building to flex slightly without the bricks cracking. It's fascinating. The history of architecture in this city is really something else. I bought this book on it a few weeks ago, big coffee table thing, full of old black-and-white photos. I haven't actually read much of it yet, but the pictures are great. My wife hates it, though, she says it takes up too much room on the table. She's been on this huge decluttering kick lately. She watched some show on Netflix about minimalism, and now she's trying to throw everything away. I came home on Tuesday and she had three garbage bags full of my old clothes sitting by the door. I mean, I know I haven't worn some of those shirts since the nineties, but still... you never know when a good flannel is gonna come in handy, right? Especially when the weather starts turning...

Sorry, I'm doing it again, aren't I? But yeah, the short answer is yes. I'm really overwhelmed. It feels like I'm losing control of my own life, and it's... it's really starting to scare me, to be honest.
Have you experienced these same symptoms of inattention and restlessness in multiple settings, such as at work, at home, and in social situations, consistently throughout your life?

Yeah, it’s really been my whole life, honestly. Everywhere I go. Like, even way back in elementary school, my teachers were already telling my parents that I couldn’t stay in my seat. I was always talking out of turn, losing my homework, and just rushing through directions before I even really understood what I was supposed to be doing. 

I remember this one teacher, Mrs. Gable in third grade... she had this huge collection of those giant pink erasers. You know the ones? They always smelled kind of weird, like rubber and chalk dust. I used to chew on the corners of them. Actually, I chewed on all my pencils, too. The yellow paint would flake off in my mouth. They don’t really make pencils like that anymore, do they? Now it’s all mechanical pencils with that tiny little lead that snaps if you press even a little bit too hard. I tried using those on the job site for marking cuts, but they are totally useless. You need a good, thick carpenter’s pencil. The flat ones, you know, so they don’t roll off the roof. I lost a really nice tape measure off a roof once. Just slid right down the pitch and smashed on the concrete driveway. It was a 35-foot Stanley FatMax, too. Those things are usually indestructible. My dad swore by Stanley tools. He had this old metal toolbox in our garage that weighed like fifty pounds, and the latch was busted so you had to carry it with both hands or all the wrenches would spill out... 

Wait, sorry. The question. My whole life. Yeah, so the teachers saw it early on, and it just... it never stopped. Whether I'm at work, at home, or out with my buddies, it's always been exactly like this.
Are you feeling like your symptoms are making it difficult for you to maintain your current job or relationships?

Yeah, I mean, like I was saying earlier, it's really threatening both of those things. At work, the missed follow-ups and all the poorly organized site coordination... it got bad enough that my employer gave me that formal warning. Sitting in his office for that was brutal. And his office is always freezing, by the way. I don't know why he keeps the AC cranked so high in there. He's got this massive glass desk, too, which just makes the whole room feel colder. I read an article once that said keeping an office cold is supposed to increase productivity, but I just end up shivering. It's like those giant computer data centers, you know? They have to keep the servers at a specific temperature so they don't overheat. My buddy Mike works in IT, and he says the noise in those server rooms is absolutely deafening. Just constant humming from the cooling fans. He actually has to wear heavy-duty ear protection just to go in there. I should probably wear ear protection more on the job site, honestly. My hearing's definitely taken a hit over the years from all the power tools. The chop saws are the worst, they have this high-pitched whine that just cuts right through you... 

Anyway, sorry. My job. Yeah, my boss is seriously concerned about my performance. And then at home... it's exactly what I mentioned before. My wife is just completely worn down from having to remind me about things I promised I would handle. It's really taking a toll on her. Like, I told her I'd fix the back gate weeks ago—the latch is totally rusted out. Speaking of rust, you wouldn't believe what the road salt around here does to the undercarriage of a truck. I had to replace the entire exhaust system on my Silverado last winter. The mechanic showed me the old pipes when he took them off, and they were literally crumbling in his hands like paper. It's a total racket, really, how much they charge for replacement parts now. 

But... yeah. Yes. I'm definitely worried I'm going to lose my job if I don't figure this out, and I hate what it's doing to my marriage.
Do you often struggle to start tasks or projects, even when you know what needs to be done?

Yeah, all the time. It's like... there's this invisible wall between me and actually doing the thing. I know exactly what the first step is, but I just sit there staring at it. Or I'll decide I need to get ready to start, which somehow turns into me cleaning out the entire center console of my truck. 

I found a bunch of old receipts in there the other day, actually. Some of the ink had completely faded off because of the heat. You know how those thermal printers work? They don't even use ink, it's just heat-sensitive paper. My uncle used to work for a company that manufactured those rolls. He'd bring home boxes of the defective ones for us to draw on when we were kids. We used to hold them up to the lightbulb in my bedroom lamp to watch the paper turn black. My mom got so mad because I accidentally left one on the lampshade and it started smoking. That lamp was this ugly brass thing she got at a garage sale. She loved going to garage sales. Every Saturday morning, she'd be up at 6 AM circling ads in the newspaper...

But, uh, yeah. Starting things is a huge problem. I just... I can't seem to get the engine turning over, you know?
Are your symptoms causing significant problems in your relationships with friends and family?

Yeah, they definitely are. Like I was saying, it's... it's causing a lot of friction. My wife, she's just exhausted from it. I tell her I'm going to take care of something, and I really mean to, but then I just don't. And she has to remind me over and over. She shouldn't have to be my manager, you know? 

Speaking of managers, the guy I report to at work, Dave... he actually sat me down a couple weeks ago. The missed follow-ups and the way I've been organizing—or not organizing—the site coordination, it's gotten bad enough that he had to express formal concern. Dave's usually a pretty laid-back guy, too. He used to manage this huge commercial development downtown before he came to our company. That project was massive, like three city blocks. They had to pour so much concrete for the foundation, they had trucks lined up around the block starting at 3 AM. You have to pour early in the summer so the concrete doesn't cure too fast in the heat. If it cures too fast, it cracks, and then you've got a whole structural nightmare on your hands. My buddy Steve poured a patio in his backyard last July right in the middle of the day, and I told him, I said, "Steve, you gotta wait till the evening or keep it wet." He didn't listen, and sure enough, two weeks later, giant hairline crack right down the middle. He tried to patch it with some epoxy filler, but you can always see the patch. It never matches the original color. Concrete's funny like that, the color depends on the exact mix of sand and aggregate...

But, uh, anyway. Yeah, my wife is worn out, and my boss is seriously worried about my work. It's a mess.
Are you having trouble completing everyday tasks, like household chores or personal care, because of your symptoms?

Yeah, chores, work tasks... it all kind of falls apart halfway through. Like, take work for example. If someone gives me a list of things to follow up on after a site walk... Site walks are usually first thing in the morning, right when the dew is still heavy. You definitely need good waterproof boots for that. I swear by my Red Wings. I've had the same pair for four years, I just keep getting them resoled. There's this old cobbler downtown, one of the last guys who actually stitches the soles by hand instead of just gluing them. Gluing is so cheap, it peels right off the second you step in deep mud. We had a site last spring that was basically a mud pit. We actually had a mini-excavator sink right up to its tracks. Took two guys and a heavy-duty tow strap to yank it out. Those tow straps are incredible, though. They're made of this woven nylon that can hold, like, thirty thousand pounds without snapping. You have to be really careful, though, because if a strap that size snaps under tension, it acts like a giant whip. It can take a guy's head clean off. I saw a safety video about that once for a logging site. Logging is a crazy industry, man. Those guys are out in the middle of nowhere...

But, uh, what was I saying? Right, the list. So I'll have this list of follow-ups from the site walk, and I'll handle the first one or two things, and then I just get pulled into something else entirely. Like the stuck excavator, or whatever else is going on. And then days later I'll find out I never sent the email, or I completely forgot to call the subcontractor back, or I just never closed out the issue. And it's the exact same thing with chores at home. I'll start doing something and just... never finish it.
Have you ever been diagnosed with or treated for attention deficit hyperactivity disorder?

No, no one's ever told me I had that. I mean, I never really went to the doctor much growing up anyway. My dad was one of those "walk it off" guys, you know? Unless a bone was sticking out, you were going to school. He worked at the auto plant for thirty-five years and I think he called in sick maybe twice. That plant closed down back in '08, which was a real shame because a lot of guys my dad's age just lost their pensions. They ended up turning the whole factory complex into these expensive loft apartments. I actually did some of the framing on that job. The original brickwork in those old factories is amazing, though. They used these solid clay bricks that you just can't find anymore. Nowadays everything is extruded and has holes in it to save weight and material. But those old solid bricks, man, they hold heat like you wouldn't believe. It makes the buildings really energy efficient in the winter, but in the summer, they turn into an absolute oven if you don't have good AC. We had to install these massive commercial HVAC units on the roof with a crane. Operating a crane that size is wild, the guy in the cab is basically using joysticks like a video game, but he's moving fifty tons of steel...

But, uh, no. To answer your question, I've never been diagnosed with anything like that. Never been treated for it, either. Just always been this way, I guess.
Have you ever had any periods in your life where your symptoms of inattention and hyperactivity were not present, or were much less severe?

Well, I mean, it's never really gone away, but it hasn't always been this bad. Like, it's been seriously disrupting my job for about two years and two months now. That's when the construction schedule changed and the hours just got completely chaotic. We started doing these split shifts to keep up with the supply chain delays. Supply chain stuff is a nightmare right now, by the way. You order a batch of electrical panels and they tell you it's a forty-week lead time. Forty weeks! How are you supposed to build a schedule around that? My buddy Mark, he's an electrician, he had to completely rewire this custom house because the homeowner decided last minute they wanted a smart home system. Those smart systems are crazy, you can control your thermostat from your phone while you're on vacation in Mexico. I went to Cabo once, back in my twenties. We rented dune buggies and drove them right on the beach. You have to lower the tire pressure so you don't get stuck in the soft sand. If you leave them fully inflated, they just dig a hole and you're buried to the axle in two seconds. It's basic physics, really, surface area and weight distribution...

But, yeah, anyway. The last two years and a couple months have been the worst of it, ever since the hours got so crazy at work. Before that, it was there, but I could kind of manage it better, you know?
Have you ever had a comprehensive evaluation for Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder?

No, I haven't. I mean, like I said, I really never went to the doctor much for anything. I think the closest thing I ever had to a real evaluation was when I had to get my DOT physical to drive the company trucks. They make you do all these tests, check your vision, your hearing, your blood pressure. Blood pressure is a big one, actually. A lot of guys in construction have terrible blood pressure because all we eat is fast food from the drive-thru or those roach coaches that pull up to the job sites. You know those food trucks? Some of them are actually pretty good now. There's this one guy, Hector, he makes these incredible al pastor tacos right on the spot. He's got the whole spit set up in the back of the truck with the pineapple on top. The acid in the pineapple actually tenderizes the pork as it cooks, it's brilliant. It's an old technique they brought over from Lebanese immigrants in Mexico, actually. They took the shawarma spit and adapted it for pork. Food history is fascinating when you really get into it. Like, did you know that tomatoes aren't originally from Italy? They're from the Americas. It's crazy to think about Italian food without tomatoes, but they didn't have them until the 1500s...

But, uh, anyway. No, I've never had a real, you know, comprehensive evaluation for this stuff. Just the basic physicals for work.
Have you ever been diagnosed with any other mental health conditions, such as depression or anxiety?

No, never anything like that. No depression, no anxiety, nothing they've ever put a name to, anyway. I mean, everybody gets stressed, right? Especially when you're trying to manage a crew of twenty guys who all think they know better than the blueprints. Last week, we had this issue where the plumbers ran a three-inch PVC pipe right through a load-bearing joist. Just drilled a massive hole right in the middle of it. I almost lost my mind. I had to call the structural engineer out, and he was furious. Those engineers, man, they don't mess around. They calculate the sheer strength of the wood, the dead load, the live load. It's all math. My nephew is actually going to college for engineering right now. He's at State, pulling all-nighters studying calculus and physics. I don't know how he does it. I tried to help him with his math homework once when he was in high school, and it looked like Greek to me. Speaking of Greek, my wife and I went to this Greek festival downtown a few years ago. The food was unbelievable. They had this stuff, baklava, layered with honey and nuts. It's so sweet it almost hurts your teeth, but you can't stop eating it. The phyllo dough they use is so thin, it's like tissue paper. I watched this documentary once on how they make it in these huge factories, stretching it out over these massive tables...

But, uh, what were we talking about? Oh, right, other conditions. No, never been diagnosed with depression or anxiety or anything like that. Just the usual stress, you know?

doctor.intent: reason for visit
doctor.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

target_item.name: Sustained_Attention_Difficulty
target_item.manifestation: What brings me in is I can start a safety briefing or a plan review trying hard to pay attention, but within minutes my mind is off on three other job problems and I miss things I know I should have caught.
target_item.reason: This is the first reply of the consultation, so I must return the chief complaint symptom code.

patient.answer:
Hey, doc. Thanks. Yeah, so... I guess what brings me in is things are just getting really bad for me at work.
